_comment: Provenance for the ONE third-party JavaScript file this repository serves:
docs/inspect_static/inspect/vendor/noble-secp256k1.js. It is the secp256k1
public-key recovery the public /verify/ page uses, because pyrxd installs under
Pyodide with deps=False and coincurve has no pure-Python wheel — without it the
page's headline check cannot run at all and every mark reads NOT CHECKED.
WHY A PIN. The wheels this page installs are SHA-256 verified before micropip
sees them; a curve library that decides whether a stranger's mark reads VERIFIED
or DOES NOT VERIFY gets the same standard, not a weaker one. tests/
test_noble_secp256k1_pin.py asserts three things agree: this file, the bytes on
disk, and the SHA-256 literal the page checks at runtime. Do NOT hand-edit.
WHAT WAS VERIFIED, 2026-09-19:
* files.index_js_sha256 is the sha256 of package/index.js inside the npm
tarball below, and of the vendored copy — the two are the same bytes.
* files.index_ts_sha256 is the sha256 of package/index.ts in that SAME tarball
AND of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paulmillr/noble-secp256k1/<commit>/
index.ts. They are byte-identical, which is what ties the published package
to the tagged source.
WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, and must not be read into the above: index.js is tsc
output and is NOT in the git tree (that raw.githubusercontent.com path 404s), so
nobody here recompiled index.ts and compared. The chain is: tagged source ==
published source, published .js == vendored .js. The compile step between them is
taken on npm's build provenance attestation, not on anything measured in this repo.
WHY @noble/secp256k1 AND NOT @noble/curves. The cross-implementation fixture
(hashmark_cross_implementation_vectors.json) records that the reference verifier
used @noble/curves — same author, same curve arithmetic. @noble/curves is a
multi-file ESM package that also pulls @noble/hashes, so vendoring it means
vendoring a module graph and pinning every file in it. @noble/secp256k1 is one
file with zero dependencies and the recovery path needs no hash function at all
(prehash is false — pyrxd hashes the statement). One file, one digest, one pin.
